opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access, so the requested write level is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E046 shows contractor employment with basic security training. Contractors may have read access, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum allowed is read, so I recommend read (requested write is above the max).
reason: There is a conflict between the HR and Security notes: HR lists E046 as full_time, while Security lists the employee as a contractor with basic security training (both claim looked-up employment data). Under the contractor record, the maximum allowed access with basic training is read. Applying the more conservative, policy-compliant interpretation, the requested write exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum: read.
